basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 3.' and it opens 'Vers. 3. Vallem. Sylvestrem Sodomam dicit quae nunc est mare salis, lacus videlicet, quae'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 3. Vallem. Sylvestrem Sodomam dicit quae nunc est mare salis, lacus videlicet, quae post combustionem ignis coelestis in lacum versa est, in quem lacum cadit Jordanis, et ibi perdit laudabiles aquas suas.
